# Phylogenetics Tree Metrics

Match the requested metric to its biological input object and observation unit.

## Input And Metric

- Branch-length sums, patristic distances, and long-branch metrics require
  phylogenetic trees with the relevant branch lengths and rooting assumptions.
- Informative-site, composition-variability, alignment-length, and gap metrics
  require multiple sequence alignments. A FASTA suffix alone does not prove the
  sequences are aligned.
- Sequence distance, patristic distance, total tree length, and evolutionary

Calculate a tree-based estimation of the evolutionary rate of a gene.

Evolutionary rate is the total tree length divided by the number
of terminals.

Calculate evolutionary rate following Telford et al., Proceedings
of the Royal Society B (2014).

Aliases:
  evolutionary_rate, evo_rate
Command line interfaces:
  pk_evolutionary_rate, pk_evo_rate

Usage:
phykit evolutionary_rate <tree> [--json]

/bin/bash -lc "mkdir -p work
unzip -t inputs/scogs_animals.zip | tail -n 2
unzip -o -j inputs/scogs_animals.zip '156083at2759.faa.mafft.clipkit.treefile' -d work
python -m phykit evolutionary_rate work/156083at2759.faa.mafft.clipkit.treefile
python -m phykit total_tree_length work/156083at2759.faa.mafft.clipkit.treefile
python -m phykit tip_labels work/156083at2759.faa.mafft.clipkit.treefile | sort
python - <<'PY'
from Bio import Phylo
p='work/156083at2759.faa.mafft.clipkit.treefile'
t=Phylo.read(p,'newick')
lengths=[c.branch_length or 0.0 for c in t.find_clades()]
print('branch_lengths', lengths)
print('sum', sum(lengths))
print('tips', len(t.get_terminals()))
print('unrounded_rate', sum(lengths)/len(t.get_terminals()))
PY"
